title: TS2Python wire (proto 1) — tick
description: Payload emitted by EL_PublishTick, i.e. EasyLanguage BarType 0 (a tick data series). Frame 2 of a 2-frame ZMQ message; frame 1 is the UTF-8 symbol topic. See wire.md and semantics.md — schema validation alone is NOT sufficient to implement a correct binding.

proto.description: Protocol version. Named `proto` rather than `v` on purpose: the superseded wire used `v` and counted up to 4, so restarting at 1 under the same key would make {"v":1} a legal opening for both protocols. A binding must refuse any frame where this key is absent or not 1, and say in the error that the DLL may predate this protocol. See wire.md.

seq.description: Per-symbol monotonic sequence, starting at 1. Shared with bar on the same symbol — both interleave on one topic, so one counter is what detects loss on that stream. A number is consumed even when the send that follows it fails, so a gap means data really was lost. Emitted as an unsigned 64-bit integer: parsers that decode JSON numbers as doubles must read this as an integer type or comparisons drift past 2^53. See semantics.md §6.

sid.description: Publisher session id — the UTC epoch MICROsecond stamped at init. A change means the publisher restarted and every seq reset, which is not message loss. Compare for equality only; never read it as a timestamp.

ts.description: DLL receive-side wall clock, UTC epoch seconds with sub-second precision. AUTHORITATIVE for tick event time. Must NOT be used for bar bucket alignment.

ts_str.description: Raw EL timestamp, format yyyy-MM/dd-HH:mm:ss (24-hour), passed through verbatim. Empty string when EL supplied none. NOT JSON-escaped by the publisher, and no longer validated by it either — the DLL used to parse this into a ts_utc field and that field is gone, so an unparseable string now reaches the binding intact. See wire.md.

el_volume.description: EasyLanguage's `Volume` reserved word, VERBATIM. On an intraday series this is up-tick share volume alone — NOT the traded quantity, despite the name. On daily and above it is total shares. The publisher deliberately performs no selection or conversion; the el_ prefix is there so a reader looks the word up instead of assuming. See semantics.md §3.4.

el_ticks.description: EasyLanguage's `Ticks` reserved word, VERBATIM. On an intraday series this is TOTAL share volume; on daily and above it is a count of ticks. This is the inverse of el_volume, which is exactly why both are shipped rather than one being chosen for you. See semantics.md §3.4.

el_upticks.description: EasyLanguage's `UpTicks` reserved word, VERBATIM. Intraday: up-tick share volume. Daily and above: total shares.

el_downticks.description: EasyLanguage's `DownTicks` reserved word, VERBATIM. Intraday: down-tick share volume. Daily and above: 0.

el_open_interest.description: EasyLanguage's `OpenInt` reserved word, VERBATIM. Always 0 for stocks and ETFs; meaningful only for futures and options.

bid.description: Bid, or null when no quote is available. EL supplies 0 from InsideBid during historical replay and for symbols that carry no quote at all (breadth indices); the publisher normalises any non-positive value to null so the wire states the absence rather than leaving every binding to remember that 0 means "absent". A binding must ALSO invalidate quotes on index/breadth symbols, which can carry live numbers that still mean nothing. See semantics.md §3.

ask.description: Ask, or null when no quote is available. Same rule as bid.
